text:
maria: Quick heads-up — p99 latency jumped after the kernel roll yesterday on prod-3. Seeing a lot more tail spikes for short-context requests. Anyone else? Repro: run replay against v2.3.6.

alex: I ran the replay this morning. p95 stable, p99 +120ms. Synthetic poisson load didn't show the same tail. My guess: KV cold misses + larger microbatch packing.

jin: We changed kernel selection heuristics: fused-attn now selected for seq<=128 and batch_width>=8. That reduces per-token time on steady-state, but it changes packing behavior (microbatch growth) and can create convoying for single-token tails. Example trace snippet: 
```
chosen_kernel: fused_attn_v2
batch_width: 12 -> 16
elapsed_ms: 1.8 (steady) / 33.2 (tail)
kv_hit: false
```

ops-bot: perf-snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/snapshots/1830124000/profile.pb.gz (contains per-request kernel, batch_width, kv_hit_ratio) :robot_face:

karen: This matches a known replay vs synthetic gap — replay preserves user prefix locality so KV gets warm and you see different batching dynamics; synthetic uniform arrivals either under- or over-estimate tails. Also note measurement windows: some of our p99 calc code uses 5m sliding buckets which hides convoys.

sam: Proposed playbook: 1) 24h real-traffic replay (7d sample) 2) synthetic bursty Poisson with configurable CV (coeff var) 3) targeted tail stress where we force microbatch knob sweeps (microbatch_size= [1,2,4,8,16]). Capture per-request: kernel_chosen, batch_width, kv_hit, queue_wait_ms.

maria: Agree. Also add a warmup phase to the replay to avoid startup bias and a cooldown to capture eviction behavior. For p99 measurement let's use 1h windows aggregated to 24h to surface long convoys.

alex: I'll add lightweight telemetry: `kernel_chosen`, `batch_width`, `kv_hit_ratio`, `queue_time_ms` to request logs and a small sampler for full CPU/GPU stacks on tail requests (limit 1 per 10k).

jin: One more detail — KV eviction TTL currently 30s on Dedicated nodes; for sporadic workloads that causes repeated misses and batch growth. Suggest testing 30/60/90s tradeoffs. Might increase memory but reduce tail.

karen: Can we also capture kernel-level timing histograms (not just end-to-end)? Need percentiles inside fused vs unfused kernels to see if fused attn has higher latency variance for certain dims.

sam: I'll schedule an overnight run with the three-phase config and the telemetry changes. Config snippet below — we should converge on these knobs: 
```
bench_config:
  phase1: {type: replay, days: 7, warmup: 10m}
  phase2: {type: synthetic, model: poisson, cv: [0.5,1.0,2.0], duration: 2h}
  phase3: {type: tail_sweep, microbatch_size: [1,2,4,8,16], duration: 1h}
  metrics: [p95,p99,p999,kv_hit_ratio,batch_width_hist]
  telemetry: [kernel_chosen,batch_width,kv_hit,queue_time_ms]
```

maria: Great. One policy note — when comparing builds, ensure kernel mapping is deterministic (seed kernel selection) or at least record mapping so we can attribute regressions to kernel changes vs batching logic.

alex: Will do. I'll push a tiny perf flag `--deterministic-kernel-map` to the bench runner and land the telemetry PR.

jin: After we collect runs, let's meet and walk traces. If p99 still regresses, plan: revert kernel change on canary and run A/B to validate.

karen: +1. Also add automated alert if p99 increases >10% for 30m with stable throughput.

sam: Scheduled: 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC. ops-bot will start the bench and dump snapshots. I'll post results and a short summary thread.

maria: Thanks team — this playbook should help us separate kernel vs batching vs KV issues and get a deterministic path to root cause. :thumbsup:
